correctness.rationale: The even subsets of the six branch points modulo complementation give the node labels; the odd subsets modulo complementation give the theta characteristics indexing tropes. Incidence is the condition that the symmetric difference is a singleton modulo complementation. This is Frobenius-equivariant and uses no choice of a rational trope. The design identity and column sums give A(3A^t−J)=12I, so the quotient is killed by 12. In an independent reconstruction I identified the target basis elements within each node orbit and summed the incidence coefficients into that orbit, retaining all sixteen source columns. Unit elimination modulo 4 followed by binary elimination on the remaining even block counts Z/2 and Z/4 factors separately; elimination modulo 3 gives one Z/3 in every class. The computation reproduces all eleven rows and the class counts; both label actions for (2,2,1,1) and (2,2,2) have orbit lengths (1^4,2^6). The groups have the same order 3072 but different dimensions modulo 2. Two distinct linears and two distinct irreducible quadratics, or three distinct irreducible quadratics, give squarefree sextic models realizing the two types over every odd finite field, including F_3.
residual_risks: Odd characteristic and the formal unsigned incidence module only; no characteristic-two extension or further fieldwise realizability is implied.

value.rationale: The formal incidence relation is canonical for the Jacobian Kummer quartic. The exact arithmetic group retains information not recorded by either individual splitting scheme, their combined orbit profiles, or even the order of the computed group. The equal-order witness is realized over every odd finite field, and the finite calculation resolves a natural complete classification rather than testing arbitrarily chosen surfaces.
residual_risks: No induced Picard, Brauer, or cohomological interpretation is established; value rests on the explicit formal arithmetic invariant.
